Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The players are already out in the middle now. Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Tanzid Hasan are the two openers for Bangladesh. Mohammad Abbas will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Bangladesh keep Pakistan under pressure - Bangladesh started brilliantly with Taskin Ahmed removing both the openers early, before Mehidy Hasan Miraz struck twice to push Pakistan firmly on the back foot. Though chances dried up a bit in the middle phase, the hosts kept things tight and never allowed the scoring rate to climb. Nahid Rana once again delivered the breakthrough when it mattered most and finished with three wickets, while Taijul Islam also claimed a three-fer despite leaking a few late sixes. Bangladesh now need a strong effort from their batters, while Pakistan will be eyeing early wickets, making the final innings nicely poised. Join us a bit for Bangladesh's second innings.

Babar fights, Sajid finishes strong - Pakistan's top order failed to make much of an impact, and they soon found themselves in trouble at 79/4. Their ace batter, Babar Azam, alongside Salman Agha, revived hopes with a crucial 63-run partnership, with Babar also bringing up a fine half-century. However, once Babar was dismissed and Salman Agha threw away a promising start, wickets continued to fall at regular intervals, with the lower order unable to contribute much. Just when Bangladesh looked set for a sizeable lead, Sajid Khan showed tremendous fight, smashing 38 off just 28 balls, including four towering sixes, to drag the deficit under 50 and keep Pakistan firmly in the contest.

Bangladesh settle for slim advantage - A late blitz from Sajid Khan has turned this Test into almost a straight shootout heading into the second innings. Bangladesh would have hoped for a much bigger lead, but they will have to settle for 46 runs, which could still end up being decisive in the context of the game. With the pitch still looking very good for batting, the hosts will now aim to set a daunting target.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session! The players have already taken their places on the field. Sajid Khan and Khurram Shahzad will continue their inning. Nahid Rana will start the proceedings after the Tea break with a slip and a gully in place. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

What to expect in the final session - With the Sylhet pitch expected to offer increasing assistance to spinners as the match progresses, Bangladesh will sense a very real opportunity to enforce a significant first-innings lead and push firmly towards a historic series sweep. Pakistan's remaining tail-enders must bat well above expectations to reduce the trail difference as much as they can. Do join us for the final session on Day 2 at 9 am GMT.

Pakistan’s tail left to fight - The lower middle order failed to offer much runs on the board. The tail-enders have got free hand to hit big and trigger the scoreline. However, Sajid Khan and Khurram Shahzad have shown a glimpse of it, just before the Tea break was called, but it would be interesting to see how they will approach in the final session on Day 2. Pakistan head into Tea at 206 for 8, still considerably behind Bangladesh's first innings total of 278. The Bangladesh bowlers have bowled with exceptional discipline throughout the second session. The spinning spearhead, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, and Taijul Islam were the difference makers in the second inning. Credit to Nahid Rana as well for breaking the crucial partnership by taking the big wicket of Babar Azam.

Lone bright spot - The return of Babar Azam provided Pakistan their one genuine moment of resistance and quality. The former skipper dug in and fought back with a gritty half-century, demonstrating the class and composure that has long made him one of the world's premier batters. His knock was a lone bright spot amid the wreckage, giving Pakistan's dressing room some hope that a competitive total was still within reach. However, the joy was short-lived. Babar was eventually dismissed for 68, and Salman Agha quickly followed, leaving Pakistan in deep trouble with four wickets intact and still trailing by a significant margin.

Bangladesh fight back - Mehidy Hasan Miraz struck early to remove captain Shan Masood, and wickets continued to tumble as Pakistan found themselves pinned under sustained pressure. Saud Shakeel became the fourth wicket to fall, with Pakistan's middle order unable to build any meaningful partnerships and the visitors wilting at 79 for 4 after 25 overs.

TEA ON DAY 2 - In this session, a total of 25 overs were bowled, where Pakistan scored 110 runs and lost 4 wickets. Pakistan resumed Day 2 on a mission, having closed the previous evening at a steady 21 for no loss, with openers Azan Awais and Abdullah Fazal having negotiated a tricky spell late on Day 1 without losing a wicket. However, Bangladesh's bowlers came out with renewed purpose after Lunch break, and the second session proved to be a damaging one for the tourists.

Disciplined bowling reaps rewards - The morning session undoubtedly belonged to the disciplined and relentless Bangladeshi bowling attack. Taskin Ahmed set the perfect tone with his crucial early inroads, while Shoriful Islam maintained immense pressure by bowling exceptionally tight, probing lines. Although Nahid Rana proved to be a touch expensive in his spell, Mehidy Hasan Miraz made up for it beautifully, returning phenomenal figures with a brilliant multi-wicket spell. Taskin and Miraz head into the lunch interval with two wickets apiece, capping off a stellar team performance. We will be back with the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT.

Babar stands firm with Salman - Amidst the falling wickets, Babar Azam has batted with absolute authority and immense composure, anchoring the crease effectively for the visitors. He finds crucial company in the highly capable Salman Agha, with the duo successfully guiding Pakistan to the Lunch break without further damage. Unbeaten on 17, their developing partnership is now the primary focal point of the match and will heavily dictate which team holds the advantage going into the afternoon session.

Top-order vulnerability exposed - While Shan Masood and Babar Azam attempted to rebuild the innings with a brief 38-run partnership, Mehidy Hasan Miraz quickly broke their resistance. The brilliant off-spinner trapped Masood in front, before dealing another massive blow by dismissing Saud Shakeel for just 8 runs. Shakeel’s lean patch of form continued as he was forced to make the long walk back to the dugout, leaving Pakistan reeling from a sudden, clinical middle-order collapse.

Bangladesh dominates a thrilling morning session - Bangladesh enjoyed a dream start to Day 2, firmly pushing Pakistan onto the back foot during a highly dramatic morning session. Resuming at an overnight score of 21 for no loss, Pakistan endured a disastrous opening period, losing both of their set openers within the first four overs of the day. Taskin Ahmed struck the first major blow by dismissing Abdullah Fazal and Azan Awais followed him back to the pavilion shortly after. This double-strike instantly erased the visitors' overnight momentum and breathed immense fire into the Bangladeshi bowling unit.
LUNCH ON DAY 2 - In this session, a total of 24 overs were bowled, where Pakistan scored 75 runs and lost 4 wickets.

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 2 - Athar Ali Khan highlights Litton Kumar Das’s magnificent batting display on a surface that offered plenty of early assistance to the seamers. Khan notes that Pakistan's bowlers set a great example by consistently targeting the crucial 4 to 6 meter length, mixing up full and short deliveries to force the batsmen into playing every ball. Khan reckons that the morning session remains highly fruitful for the bowling side. Khan advises the Bangladeshi attack to exploit these favorable conditions. While he points out that Nahid Rana can trouble the batters with his extra pace, he stresses that Shoriful Islam and Taskin Ahmed must remain disciplined and relentlessly target those good areas to capitalize on the seam movement available.

Khurram Shahzad is up for a chat - Khurram Shahzad says that the bowling unit's strong initial effort and early breakthroughs were key in restricting the opponents under 300. Khurram Shahzad admits to feeling a very faint edge off his own bowling against Litton Das, which led to a brief, uncertain discussion with teammates Mohammad Rizwan and Agha Salman about a potential sound. Shahzad observes that this pitch lacks the cracks and uneven bounce seen in Dhaka, explaining that his primary strategy with the new ball is to consistently hit the seam to maximize any available assistance from the surface.

A word from the Bangladesh camp, Litton Das  - Litton Das reflects on a challenging entry to the crease where difficult batting conditions left him momentarily uncertain after a flurry of wickets fell around him. Das mentions that he opted for a high-risk, aggressive approach, recognizing that the tail-enders could not be expected to shoulder the entire scoring burden. Das adds that his primary instruction to the lower-order batters was simply to occupy the crease and face as many deliveries as possible, confident that he could handle the run-scoring if he remained at the wicket. Das credits Taskin Ahmed, Taijul Islam, and especially Shoriful Islam for providing crucial, gritty support during those game-changing lower-order partnerships.

A pivotal day that will shape the Test - As we look ahead to today's play, the stakes could not be higher, as Day 2 will undoubtedly be the primary turning point in this match's trajectory. This day is absolutely critical in the grand context of the game. A heavy, authoritative response from the Pakistani batting lineup will systematically deflate the hosts, tire out their primary weapons, and force Bangladesh onto the back foot. On the flip side, if the Bangladeshi bowlers can hit their lengths early on this fresh morning surface, extract movement, and trigger a swift batting collapse, they will instantly catapult their country into a pole position to dictate terms. Every run scored and every wicket taken today will carry immense weight, and neither side can afford a single session of complacency if they wish to seize ultimate control of this Test.
